newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela holds Spaniard, Brazilian on drug charge.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela holds Spaniard, Brazilian on drug charge.

text.p: Venezuelan police said on Tuesday they had arrested two women, a Spaniard and a Brazilian, on the Caribbean island Margarita, on charges of trying to smuggle cocaine out of the country.

Spaniard Alicia Valdiviejas, 48, and Brazilian Nila Rosa Dos Santos, 38, were arrested on Monday night at Margarita Island airport carrying 23 pounds (10 kg) of cocaine, according to Lt. Col. Fernando Fernandez of the National Guard.
Fernandez said the two women, who were planning to travel to the Spanish island of Tenerife, were carrying the drugs in 38 packages hidden under their clothes.

Margarita Island, which lies just off Venezuela's northeast coast, is a major tourist attraction, drawing about 200,000 foreign visitors each year. While not a major drug producer, Venezuela has become a popular transit point for drugs from Colombia bound for the United States and Europe.
